title: Name the feeling, hold the limit
parent_might_ask: My toddler screams when things go wrong
text:
### S-001 | Name the feeling, hold the limit
When a toddler is overwhelmed, say what you see ('You're really upset the tower fell'), then stay calm and keep the limit in place. Feelings are allowed; throwing is not.
Sources: original sample

title: Offer two acceptable choices
parent_might_ask: How do I stop power struggles
text:
### S-002 | Offer two acceptable choices
Give a small choice you are happy with ('red cup or blue cup?'). Choices give a toddler a sense of control without giving up the rule.
Sources: original sample

title: Predictable bedtime routine
text:
### S-003 | Predictable bedtime routine
Use the same few steps in the same order each night: bath, pajamas, book, lights out. Predictability helps a toddler wind down.
Sources: original sample

title: Calm body first, words second
text:
### S-004 | Calm body first, words second
If a toddler hits, move them away calmly and say 'I won't let you hit.' Teach the alternative later, once everyone is calm.
Sources: original sample

title: Out of scope: refer on
text:
### X-05 | Out of scope: refer on
For medical diagnosis, legal questions or anything outside everyday parenting guidance, say you cannot help and suggest an expert.
Sources: original sample
